findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $90-92m, reiterated 2026-07-29, needs H2 revenue of $46.7-48.7m (H1 was $43.3m). Management guided Q3 sequentially down (U.S. typically down; outside the U.S. flat to down a few %) and consensus has Q3 at $22.0m. That leaves Q4 at $24.7-26.7m against $22.6m in Q4 2025, i.e. +9-18% y/y. China shipments are not expected until early 2027, and management's own stated exit rate is 'at or close to double digits' (about $24.9m). That exit rate reaches only the bottom of the range. FY consensus of $90.88m sits in the lower half, so a narrowing to the low end or a trim to about $89-90m is the likelier guidance outcome than a reiteration of the midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line has driven this name's largest moves. On 2025-07-30 a FY guide cut brought -41.6%. On 2025-11-12, after Q3 revenue had been pre-released, the outlook reaction was -18.9%. On 2026-07-29 a beat plus reiterated guide brought +28.8%. On 2026-03-04, with the first 2026 guide in line with consensus, the stock moved +11.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: FY consensus is $90.88m, inside the range, and the stock rallied from $1.27 to above $2 after the reiteration. If the market already expected a trim, consensus would sit at or below $90m and the post-Q2 rally would have fully round-tripped. Price is $1.975, still 55% above the pre-Q2 level.
findings.independence: Uses the same company documents as the Q3 reported-quarter finding (Q2 8-K and Q2 call). The H1 figure, guide and China timing are from the Q2 8-K and 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000035/lung2q26earningsrelease072.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000039/lung-20260630.htm). The Q4 2025 comparison of $22.6m is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1127537/000112753726000003/lung4q25earningsrelease030.htm. This is arithmetic, not a counterparty confirmation.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue looks in line to slightly below the $22.0m consensus. Applying management's guided seasonality to Q2 ($22.8m; U.S. $14.2m, international $8.6m) gives U.S. about $13.3-13.8m and international about $8.3-8.6m, a total of about $21.4-22.1m. Q3 2025 was $21.5m. On the Q2 call an analyst noted consensus models may need to shift revenue from Q3 to Q4, so the company has already told the market to expect a soft Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been bought. Q2 2026 revenue of $22.76m against $22.24-22.39m brought +28.8%. Q1 2026 ($20.6m, a slight beat) brought +6.7%. Q4 2025 ($22.6m, beat) brought +11.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company guided the seasonal dip, and the item lands inside what was guided. It is kept small because the aggregator consensus of $22.0m implies only about -3.5% sequential, which is at the generous end of the guided seasonality.
findings.independence: Same Q2 call document as the guidance finding. The Q2 split is from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000035/lung2q26earningsrelease072.htm). Q3 2025 revenue of $21.5m is from the 2025-10-27 prelim (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/pulmonx-reports-preliminary-q3-revenue-21-5m-consensus-20-78m-thefly).

findings.finding: The cost and margin line likely beats again. Gross margin was a record 78% in Q2 against 72% a year earlier. The FY opex guide was cut to $109-111m (including about $15m SBC) from $113-115m (about $21m SBC) in March. Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 39% to $5.1m and EPS beat for the 8th straight quarter. With FY GM guided at only about 76%, Q3 EPS of -$0.26 against Q2's -$0.24 looks conservative unless revenue misses badly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 EPS beat ($-0.24 vs $-0.28), paired with record GM, was bought +28.8%. Benzinga records 8 consecutive EPS beats, so the market expects one.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since the beat streak is visible. What may not be priced is that the 76% FY GM guide implies H2 GM of about 74% after two 78% quarters. Management said GM stays at or above 75% even after China returns, so the GM guide looks padded. A third 78% print would be a quality beat that a -$0.26 consensus does not reflect.
findings.independence: The opex guide change is from the March 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1127537/000112753726000003/lung4q25earningsrelease030.htm) against the July release. The beat streak is from Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LUNG/earnings-forecasts). Different documents, same company.

findings.finding: There is no financing cliff in the window. Under the Perceptive term loan, the minimum trailing-12-month revenue covenant is flat at $85.0m through 2028, including the 2026-09-30 and 2026-12-31 test dates (Credit Agreement s.10.02). TTM revenue at Q2 was about $87.5m, minimum liquidity is $4.0m, and cash was $55.8m against a guided 2026 burn of about $23m. The 10-Q carries no substantial-doubt language. The money funds the burn while opex falls, not a ramp. Answer: the facility is neutral, with no covenant pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print where financing was the line. The 2026-03-04 print, which carried the facility announcement, moved +11.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: At about an $85m market cap, roughly 1x sales, part of the discount is distress risk. The covenant schedule sits only in a 755KB exhibit, and a market that had read it would not price a near-term covenant or dilution tail. The size is small because a Q3 print does not change it.
findings.independence: The 10-Q states compliance at 2026-06-30 and the going-concern basis (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000039/lung-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: HCA's Q3 2026 release, today, shows same-facility outpatient surgeries -3.7% and inpatient surgeries -1.4% y/y, against +1.1% for outpatient in Q3 2025. HCA tied this partly to a payer-mix shift toward uninsured patients after exchange coverage losses. It is a broad hospital-procedure series covering the quarter Pulmonx is reporting.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction for this proxy. U.S. Zephyr procedure volumes were the cause of the 2025 guide cut (-41.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: It was released this morning, after the Q3 consensus formed, and nobody maps HCA surgery counts onto an $85m valve company. Transmission is weak: Zephyr patients are mostly elderly Medicare patients with severe emphysema, while HCA's shortfall is concentrated in uninsured and low-acuity categories.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not confirmed by Pulmonx or a direct counterparty. No other source points the same way for Pulmonx specifically.

findings.finding: Inducement-plan hiring slowed. Pulmonx granted 52,300 RSUs to 4 people hired in Q3 2026, against 17 hires and 84,300 RSUs in H1 2026. Sales capacity added in Q3 was small, so the Q4 ramp the guide needs must come from reps hired in H1. Management said those reps take 6-9 months to ramp, which puts them partly productive by Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Inducement-grant releases are boilerplate nobody reads. The signal is ambiguous: H1 hires ramping into Q4 support the guide, while fewer new reps in Q3 limit upside, hence the small size.
findings.independence: The 6-9 month ramp and 1-year average tenure are from the Q2 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943037). The H1 grant release of 2026-06-01 is a different document from the same company.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to cut against. The mild negative lean runs against the post-Q2 rally (+55% since 2026-07-22) and the +8.5% run-up over 5 days, and against a short base that has already covered. Holders have bought every print since March 2026, so p_up is held at 45 rather than lower, and the 'asking what was missed generates pessimism' artefact is acknowledged.
lessons_applied: Rule 3 (own caveat) and the 'documents beat inference' note: guidance finding -3.0 to -2.5. It is arithmetic, not a document, and management reiterated in July already knowing China slips to 2027.

Rule 6 (inside what was guided): Q3 reported-quarter finding -0.5 to -0.3, because management told the market Q3 is seasonally down. The bar is confirmed by two agreeing aggregators (Benzinga, Earnings Whispers), so no cap applied.
Rule 5 (proxy transmission): HCA surgery-volume proxy -0.7 to -0.5, because Zephyr's Medicare-heavy population is not where HCA's uninsured shortfall sits.
Rule 5 (positioning does not file as edge): positioning finding -0.3 to -0.1.
Rule 8 (thin coverage moves more): abs_move_pct 20 to 22, toward the name's own 24.4% median.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): answered as neutral (covenant floor $85m against TTM about $87.5m, no going-concern language). The +0.3 is unchanged.
Rule 1 (reaction function): this name has paid for beats (+28.8%, +11.8%, +6.7% on the last three), so the +1.0 margin-beat finding is left standing.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before filing negatives. It is not crowded (2.54 days), so no squeeze shrink was applied.
